title: Traffic-simulator-driven acceptance plan and go-live checklist for hosted inference lanes
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: This ticket captures the PRD and operational readiness checklist for validating chat/completions/embeddings/rerank hosted endpoints using an automated traffic simulator. The goal is to prove behavioral contracts (latency, cost, quality, degradations) against representative production traffic shapes prior to broad launch. The acceptance gates are quantitative and reproducible via the simulator harness. Non-functional behavior (failover, burst, quotas) must be validated alongside quality-eval checks against canary prompt suites.
background: Recent launches exposed edge regressions when production traffic mixes short chat turns and long-completion batches simultaneously. We will use a configurable traffic simulator to synthesize multi-tenant mixing, KV-cache warmup profiles, and prefix reuse to exercise runtime batching and routing policies. This effort bridges PM requirements and ENG test harnesses so sign-off is objective.
goals: Establish deterministic acceptance gates expressible as simulator scenarios
Catch regressions in throughput/latency and embedding similarity when models or runtime kernels change
Provide a repeatable checklist for SRE/ENG to run pre-cutover
Define rollback triggers and canary slicing strategy tied to simulator metrics
out_of_scope: Changes to billing or pricing models
Large-scale multi-region DR exercises (will be follow-up)
success_metrics: 95th percentile request latency within lane SLOs across 10 simulator runs
Embedding similarity AUC degradation <= 0.5% vs baseline on eval set
No increase in unit cost > 8% when running realistic batch mixes
acceptance_criteria: Traffic simulator scenario 'mixed-tenant-peak' run 10 times without SLO violations: 99th percentile tail latency meets target
Simulator-run traces show KV cache hit-rate >= configured threshold for warm-start scenarios
Quality regression suite (canary prompts) shows generation score delta <= threshold (documented per model)
Autoscaling and burst policies observed to respond within configured time windows in simulator; no request dropped due to misconfiguration
Rate-limiter and quota enforcement validated under simulated abusive clients; exceed actions match policy (429 vs throttled queue)
launch_checklist: 1) Simulator harness PR merged and pinned to release tag (link in comments)
2) Baseline golden-run recorded (artifact uploaded) for all lanes and models
3) ENG runs full simulator suite and posts results to release dashboard
4) SRE validates canary routing policies and fallback chains (region/model-level)
5) PM approves quality/regression report and sign-off matrix
6) Design verifies UX error messages and rate-limit copy for developer docs
7) Security review complete and compliance checklist signed
8) Rollout playbook published with automated rollback triggers wired
9) Post-launch monitoring dashboard and alert thresholds configured and tested
10) Stakeholder go/no-go call scheduled and recorded
rollout_plan: Phase A: 5% tenant canary for 48 hours using simulator-verified slices. Monitor telemetry for quality and SLO regressions. Phase B: 25% for 24 hours with expanded traffic shapes. Phase C: 100% after sustained green and no critical alerts for 72 hours. Automatic rollback if any simulator-backed metric crosses failure thresholds (defined under acceptance criteria).
risks: Simulator fidelity: synthesized traffic may not capture rare emergent patterns
False sense of security if golden baseline is stale relative to production model updates
Interference from unrelated infra changes during canary window
Overfitting acceptance thresholds to simulator artifacts rather than user-observed failures
decisions: Use 'mixed-tenant-peak' scenario as the canonical gate for go/no-go
Accept up to 8% unit cost increase during initial launch if quality holds and latency remains within SLO
Require per-model regression thresholds defined and owned by Applied ML for each PRD
notes: Linked artifacts: Confluence design doc https://confluence.company/hosted-api/traffic-sim; Simulator repo PR #842; Release dashboard: https://dash.company/releases/hosted-2026-03
